name: Thematic Analysis
description:
Thematic analysis is a qualitative analytical method for identifying and interpreting patterns of meaning across a body of data. Researchers become familiar with the material, code relevant features, develop candidate themes and progressively refine their interpretation.

A theme is more than a frequently mentioned topic: it captures a meaningful pattern relevant to the research question.
whenToUse: Use thematic analysis when working with qualitative material such as interviews, diary entries, open survey responses or observational notes and when the research question concerns recurring patterns of experience or meaning.
steps: Become familiar with the complete dataset.
Group related codes into candidate themes.
Review themes against the coded extracts and wider dataset.
Refine the boundaries and meaning of each theme.
Develop an interpretation supported by appropriate evidence.
lookOutFor: Themes do not simply *'emerge'* independently of the researcher; analysis involves interpretation.
Frequency alone does not determine importance.
Maintain a traceable relationship between claims, codes and original material.

resources.citation: Braun, V. & Clarke, V. (2006). “Using Thematic Analysis in Psychology.” *Qualitative Research in Psychology*, 3(2), 77–101.
Braun, V. & Clarke, V. (2022). *Thematic Analysis: A Practical Guide*. Sage.
